issues.legal_issue: A landholder’s obligation to submit a land return includes land that is otherwise exempt from the substantive operation of the land-ceiling law.
material_facts: A company owning a sugarcane factory challenged the interpretation that it had to submit a return of its lands.
The statutory scheme included categories of exempt land, while the return provision expressly included exempt land.
The return requirement was intended to give the authorities an account of all lands held by persons in the State.
issues.conclusion: The return obligation extends to all land held by the landholder, including exempt land; the appeal was dismissed and the landholder was directed to submit the return.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Madhya Pradesh Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1960 must be read in its setting and in light of its purpose. Although Section 3 exempts specified lands from the Act’s provisions and Sections 2(d) and 7 concern ceiling area and the land a person may hold, the broad wording of Section 9 serves the objective of giving authorities an account of all lands, whether exempt or not. No earlier cases are cited. The Court noted that failure to file could contravene Section 10 and might attract a penalty under Section 10(2), but did not decide whether a penalty should be imposed.

predicates.land_ceiling_return_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether a landholder must submit a return under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.landholder_holds_land: The landholder holds land that is subject to the scheme’s return requirement.
predicates.return_scheme_covers_exempt_land: The scheme’s return requirement is intended to disclose held land even when that land is exempt from the scheme’s substantive operation.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a land-ceiling return, the landholder holds land, and the return scheme covers exempt land, the landholder must report all held land, including exempt land.
